what_source_actually_states: The article is R. Quintanilla, 'A condition on the delay parameters in the one-dimensional dual-phase-lag thermoelastic theory', Journal of Thermal Stresses 26:713-721 (2003), DOI 10.1080/713855996, printed on the Taylor & Francis cover page along with the citation line and, separately, in the article footer. The abstract (p. 713) states: 'In this theory two delay parameters ty and tq are considered. We prove that when ty > tq/2 the solutions decay exponentially and when ty < tq/2 there exist unstable solutions. These results suggest that ... we must assume that the inequality ty > tq/2 holds.' The same page fixes the truncation that the condition belongs to: 'We consider the theory developed by taking the Taylor series in both sides of Eq. (1) into account and retaining terms up to the second order in tq but only to the first order in ty. One obtains Eq. (3) (with b = 0).' Eq. (4) on p. 714 writes the operators as ^f = f + ty f_dot and ~f = f + tq f_dot + (tq^2/2) f_ddot, i.e. second order in the flux lag and first order in the gradient lag; Eq. (7) repeats the same truncation in nondimensional form. Section 3 on p. 715 proves exponential stability under the condition, written there as ty > tq/2 = Eq. (11). So all three parts of the manuscript's sentence - who derived it, for which truncation, and why it is quoted as the DPL stability condition - are stated on the pages read.
